bourse

bourse is the market-data connector of the ORCHESTRA analytics framework: it fetches cryptocurrency market data (OHLCV candles, order books, 24-hour tickers) from public exchange APIs and emits it as a contract-typed, provenance-labelled result. It is the trading-domain counterpart of the terroir geo-data collector.

Every external fact – a symbol, a price tick size, a fee, a column’s unit – is recorded in a provenance registry and treated as unverified until it has been diffed against the exchange’s own catalogue (the Independent Oracle Principle). An ungrounded fact triggers a refusal rather than a silently wrong number. For a trading system that is risk control, not bookkeeping: an unverified tick size or fee is a number that loses money.

bourse supplies market data only. It gives no financial or trading advice.

Related packages

  • cryptoQuotes returns OHLC market data from major cryptocurrency exchanges as xts series, with sentiment indicators and interactive charts.
  • crypto2 downloads cryptocurrency information and daily historical prices from CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko.
  • binancer is a client for the Binance public REST API, for data collection, portfolio management and trading.

bourse reads Binance’s public endpoints too, but each result carries the grounding status of the facts it rests on (symbol, tick size, fee, units), checked against the exchange’s own catalogue, and it returns a refusal instead of a value when a fact has not been checked.

Installation 

pak::pak("max578/bourse")

Usage

Each verb returns either a grounded result object or a bourse_refusal. Here we parse recorded fixtures offline (the live path uses the suggested httr2).

library(bourse)

candles <- cbind(
  open_time = c(1.5e12, 1.5e12 + 86400000),
  open = c(100, 102), high = c(105, 106), low = c(99, 101),
  close = c(102, 104), volume = c(1200, 1500))

bourse_ohlcv("BTCUSDT", interval = "1d", candles = candles)
#> <market_series> BTCUSDT @ binance [1d]  2 rows  [[unverified]]

bourse_orderbook("BTCUSDT", depth = list(
  bids = list(c("100.0", "1.5")), asks = list(c("100.1", "1.0"))))
#> <order_book> BTCUSDT @ binance  1 bids / 1 asks  [[unverified]]

bourse_ticker("BTCUSDT", ticker = list(
  symbol = "BTCUSDT", lastPrice = "100.0", openPrice = "98.0",
  highPrice = "101.0", lowPrice = "97.0", volume = "1200",
  quoteVolume = "118800", openTime = 1.5e12, closeTime = 1.5e12 + 86400000))
#> <market_ticker> BTCUSDT @ binance  last=100  24h=NA%  [[unverified]]

A result is [unverified] until the catalogue-diff oracle has grounded the facts it rests on; a consumer on a live order path gates on the grounding label.

Grounding: the catalogue-diff oracle

bourse_catalogue_diff() is the only operation that grounds a fact. It diffs the asserted facts against the exchange’s own /exchangeInfo catalogue and grounds those that agree with a real date. By default it grounds the multi-symbol core universe (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, BNBUSDT, SOLUSDT).

bourse_fact_status("binance")
#>    source n_facts n_grounded n_unverified
#> 1 binance      10          0           10

Known gap: the fee schedule

bourse reads public, anonymous endpoints only. The maker/taker fee_schedule is sourced from the authenticated /sapi/v1/asset/tradeFee endpoint, which would introduce an API-credential surface; it is deliberately not implemented. That fact stays [unverified] in the registry rather than substituting a documentation default the package cannot diff against the account’s actual fee tier. See SECURITY.md.
